candidate_relations.reason: Acute urticaria implies duration <6 weeks and is a distinct subtype from CSU (>6 weeks, spontaneous). The clinical record describes onset 7 hours post-vaccination with no prior history, which superficially suggests acute urticaria; however, the reference diagnosis is CSU. Labeling it 'acute' directly conflicts with the chronic temporal classification required by CSU.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Acute urticaria vs. Chronic Spontaneous Urticaria — incompatible temporal subtype

candidate_relations.reason: CSU is defined by the absence of an identifiable external trigger. Attributing the urticaria/angioedema to an allergic reaction to the vaccine assigns a specific extrinsic etiology, which is incompatible with the 'spontaneous' component of CSU. The reference diagnosis implies the vaccine exposure may have unmasked or coincided with CSU rather than being the direct allergic cause.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Vaccine-triggered allergic reaction — identifies an extrinsic cause/trigger, conflicting with the 'spontaneous' (no identifiable cause) classification of CSU

candidate_relations.reason: Urticaria is the parent diagnostic entity encompassing CSU, but it lacks the required temporal (chronic, >6 weeks) and etiological (spontaneous, no identifiable trigger) qualifiers that define CSU as a distinct subtype.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Generic 'Urticaria' is the parent category; missing the 'chronic' and 'spontaneous' specifiers required by CSU

case_quality_flags: Reference diagnosis of CSU is clinically debatable: symptom onset 7 hours post-vaccination with no prior urticaria history more typically supports acute urticaria or vaccine-triggered urticaria rather than CSU, which requires >6 weeks of recurrent episodes; the record does not document chronicity.
Absence of prior urticaria history and clear temporal trigger (vaccination) conflicts with standard CSU diagnostic criteria — case may reflect an editorial decision to classify vaccine-unmasked CSU.
